Regulation: B.C. Reg. 114/2026
Made under: Provincial Sales Tax Act
Published in: No. 13 – B.C. Regs. 110 to 124, July 14, 2026
Deposit date: July 9, 2026

B.C. Reg. 114/2026, deposited July 9, 2026, under thePROVINCIAL SALES TAX ACT[sections 236, 241 and 246]. Order in Council 295/2026, approved and ordered July 9, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, effective October 1, 2026, (a)	the Provincial Sales Tax Exemption and Refund Regulation, B.C. Reg. 97/2013 is amended as set out in Schedule 1, and (b)	the Provincial Sales Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 96/2013, is amended as set out in Schedule 2. —B. BAILEY,Minister of Finance; A. DIX,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. 1	Section 60 of the Provincial Sales Tax Exemption and Refund Regulation, B.C. Reg. 97/2013, is amended by striking out "Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act Regulation" and substituting "Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Regulation". 2	The following section is added: Exemption in relation to legal services that  relate to another jurisdiction 79.1(1)	Subject to subsection (2), legal services are exempt from tax imposed under section 126 (1)[tax if legal services provided in British Columbia]of the Act if the legal services relate to a jurisdiction other than British Columbia. (2)	A purchaser or recipient of legal services is exempt from tax imposed under section 126 (1) of the Act in relation to that portion of the purchase price which is for legal services that relate to a jurisdiction other than British Columbia if part of the legal services relates to a jurisdiction other than British Columbia. (3)	For the purposes of this section, legal services relate to a jurisdiction other than British Columbia in the same manner as legal services relate to British Columbia within the meaning of section 127 (2) of the Act. 3	Section 81 (1) (b) is amended by striking out "Indians" and substituting "First Nation individuals". 4	Part 4 is amended by adding the following Divisions: Division 4.1 – Accounting Services Exemption in relation to accounting services  that relate to another jurisdiction 82.1(1)	Subject to subsection (2), accounting services are exempt from tax imposed under section 129.11 (1)[tax on accounting services provided in British Columbia]of the Act if the accounting services relate to a jurisdiction other than British Columbia. (2)	A purchaser or recipient of accounting services is exempt from tax imposed under section 129.11 (1) of the Act in relation to that portion of the purchase price which is for accounting services that relate to a jurisdiction other than British Columbia if part of the accounting services relates to a jurisdiction other than British Columbia. (3)	For the purposes of this section, accounting services relate to a jurisdiction other than British Columbia in the same manner as accounting services relate to British Columbia in relation to a matter referred to in section 129.11 (2) (a) to (h) of the Act. Exemptions in relation to accounting services 82.11The following are exempt from tax imposed under Division 4.1 of Part 5 of the Act:

minutes_briefs.title: BC PST exemption for legal and accounting services tied to other jurisdictions takes effect Oct 1
minutes_briefs.summary: Starting October 1, 2026, British Columbia will exempt legal and accounting services from the Provincial Sales Tax (PST) when those services relate to a jurisdiction other than BC. This means if a lawyer or accountant in BC provides services for a matter that is connected to another province or country, that portion of the bill will not be taxed. The change also updates some wording in the regulations, such as replacing 'Indians' with 'First Nation individuals'.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Review your invoices for legal or accounting services that relate to other jurisdictions and confirm your provider applies the PST exemption after October 1, 2026.

key_dates.label: BC PST exemption for out-of-province legal and accounting services takes effect
